{"rule": "Return this JSON object with the rule field unchanged and a new passage of about 250 words in the text field.", "text": "The bridge was iron, or had been, and the river had taken most of the paint and some of the rails. It began on their side with two stone posts and ended on hers with two more, and between them the deck sagged in the middle like a sentence that has lost confidence in its own ending.

The woman reached her posts before they reached theirs. She did not step onto the bridge. She stood with one hand resting on the stone and waited, and Tomas understood that she would go on waiting, that the crossing was not hers to make.

"You go," the boy said.

"Why me?"

"Because she's looking at you."

She was. Not unkindly. The way one looks at a door one has knocked on, listening for footsteps that may or may not come.

Tomas put his foot on the first plank. It held. He put the other down and the whole structure gave a low note, not a groan but something closer to a chord, and he felt it travel up through his shins and settle somewhere under his ribs. He thought of the glove, or the paper, whatever she had been turning. He thought he might know what it said.

Halfway across he stopped and looked down. The water was moving in two directions at once, or seemed to be, the surface running downstream while something darker underneath ran the other way. He did not look long.

When he looked up she had taken her hand from the post. She held the folded thing out toward him, arm straight, and he saw now that it was neither glove nor paper but a photograph, and that the face in it, small and grey at that distance, was turned away.

Behind him the boy said nothing, and that silence was the loudest thing on the river."}
